title: Morning Edition
intro: Big moves from Anthropic and OpenAI dominate today’s AI news, with developments spanning moderation, research and corporate strategy. Expect coverage of a new astrophysics milestone alongside cultural and market signals.

items.headline: OpenAI defends firing three safety researchers
items.aiSummary: The Verge reports OpenAI stands by its decision to fire three safety researchers after an investigation found a "significant breach of trust." The company named Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni and said they violated "clear policies on handling sensitive information."

items.title: Anthropic's Claude Science creates the first complete ultraviolet map of the sky
items.summary: Astrophysicist Brice Ménard of Johns Hopkins University used Anthropic's Claude Science to map the entire sky in ultraviolet light for the first time. items.why: It shows generative AI techniques applied to large-scale scientific data can produce useful, quantified results.
items.headline: Claude Science creates first full ultraviolet sky map
items.aiSummary: The Decoder reports astrophysicist Brice Ménard used Anthropic’s Claude Science to map the entire sky in ultraviolet light for the first time. AI agents downloaded data from multiple space missions, calibrated it, and filled gaps using inpainting (a method for filling missing data); predictions averaged about ten percent deviation from actual measurements.

items.headline: Nvidia-backed Firmus reportedly scraps $5 billion IPO
items.aiSummary: Yahoo Finance reports that Firmus, backed by Nvidia, has reportedly scrapped a planned $5 billion initial public offering. The report indicates the IPO will not proceed as previously planned.
